title: Fabrication of a paper-based colorimetric molecular test for SARS-CoV-2
author: Wang, Dextre, et al.

steps.title: Decontaminate workspace and cut paper
steps.instruction: Spray all workbench surfaces and spray pipettes with RNase AWAY, wipe thoroughly, and allow to dry. Work in separate rooms for device fabrication and sample loading to avoid cross‑contamination. Pre‑cut chromatography paper (Ahlstrom‑Munksjö Grade 222, catalog 22282020) into 5 mm × 6 mm pieces.

steps.title: Prepare 2X LAMP reagent mix
steps.instruction: In a PCR hood, combine the following reagents to a final volume of 1 mL: 100 µL 1000 mM KCl (P9541, Sigma‑Aldrich), 160 µL 100 mM MgSO₄ (M2773, Sigma‑Aldrich), 280 µL 10 mM dNTPs (N0447, NEB), 10.8 µL 120 U/µL Bst 2.0 DNA polymerase (M0537M, NEB), 40 µL 15 U/µL WarmStart® RTx reverse transcriptase (M0380S, NEB), 20 µL 25 mM phenol red (P3532, Sigma‑Aldrich), 2.8 µL 100 mM dUTP (FERR0133, Thermo Scientific), 0.4 µL 1 U/µL Antarctic thermolabile UDG (M0372S, NEB), 100 µL 20 % Polysorbate 20 (278632500, Thermo Scientific), and 286 µL nuclease‑free water (4387936, Thermo Scientific).

steps.title: Adjust pH of 2X mix and store
steps.instruction: Add 1–2 µL of 1 M KOH to the 2X LAMP mix to reach pH ≈ 7.5–8.0 (red but not pink). No precise pH is required. After adjustment, aliquot and store the 2X mix at –20 °C.

steps.title: Assemble complete paper LAMP mix
steps.instruction: Combine the following in a clean tube to a total of 200 µL: 125 µL 2X LAMP mix, 25 µL 10X primer mix (final concentrations: 16 µM FIP/BIP, 2 µM F3/B3, 4 µM Loop F/B), 1 µL 5 M betaine (B0300‑5VL, Sigma‑Aldrich) for a final 20 mM, optional 3.13 µL 40 mg/mL BSA (A2153, Sigma‑Aldrich) for a final 0.626 mg/mL, 36 µL 689 mg/mL trehalose (182550250, Thermo Scientific), and 9.2 µL nuclease‑free water. Mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Load mix onto paper pads and dry
steps.instruction: Using a micro‑pH electrode (e.g., model 11‑747‑328, Fisher Scientific), adjust the pH of the complete mix to 8.0 with 0.1 M KOH. Lay the pre‑cut Grade 222 pads on a clean surface inside the PCR hood. Pipette 30 µL of the complete mix onto each pad, then let the pads dry at room temperature for 60 min. After drying, collect the pads into a clean 0.5 mL centrifuge tube (05‑408‑129, Fisher Scientific) or a resealable 1″ × 1″ plastic bag (S‑12250, Uline).

steps.title: Reconstitute pads with samples
steps.instruction: Again spray the bench with RNase AWAY and wipe clean. Retrieve DNA/RNA templates or heat‑inactivated virus from the freezer. Lay the dried pads on a clean surface (optionally on a new transparency film, 617993, Office Depot). For negative controls, add 25 µL nuclease‑free water or saliva to each pad, handling gently to avoid washing out reagents. Place the negative pads into a clean container using forceps. Dilute the template to the desired concentration, then add 25 µL of the diluted template to separate pads for the test samples. Store the positive pads in a clean container. Clean the workspace before proceeding to imaging.

steps.title: Scan pads before incubation
steps.instruction: Arrange all reconstituted pads on a tabletop scanner and acquire a scan at time 0 min.

steps.title: Incubate pads at 65 °C and image
steps.instruction: Pre‑heat a microbiological incubator (or water bath) to 65 °C. Place the pads inside, ensuring they are well separated for uniform heating. At desired intervals (typically every 30 min), remove the pads and scan them again. Continue until the final time point (e.g., 60 min).

steps.title: Dispose of used pads
steps.instruction: After the final scan, discard all reaction pads in biohazard waste.

steps.title: Optional: Validate amplification by gel
steps.instruction: Transfer each pad to a clean 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, add 100 µL Buffer EB (catalog 19086, Qiagen), and submerge overnight to elute nucleic acids. Run the eluate on a 2 % agarose gel alongside a DNA ladder; positive pads should show the characteristic ladder‑like LAMP pattern, while negative pads show no band.
